name: anchored
whatItDemonstrates: Two independently managed toast systems in one demo: a copy button that pops an arrowed 'Copied' toast anchored next to itself via positionerProps.anchor, and a separate bottom-right stacked toast queue fed by a second button.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — toasts live in two module-scope Toast.createToastManager() instances wired to two separate Toast.Providers; the only local state is a useState `copied` boolean on the copy button, set true on click and reset by the toast's onClose callback
nonTrivialInteractions: two module-scope managers (anchoredToastManager, stackedToastManager) each back their own <Toast.Provider>, so anchored and stacked toasts render through independent Portal/Viewport trees

CopyButton adds a toast with positionerProps { anchor: buttonRef.current, sideOffset: 10 } so a Toast.Positioner + Toast.Root + Toast.Arrow tree docks to the button, plus timeout: 1500 for auto-dismiss
the added toast's onClose callback flips `copied` back to false, which re-enables the rendered Button (disabled={copied}) and un-disables the surrounding Tooltip
the trigger is a Tooltip.Trigger rendered as a Button (render prop) with closeOnClick={false}; Tooltip.Root is disabled while `copied` is true so the tooltip does not compete with the toast

the stacked queue maps toasts into Toast.Root > Toast.Content > Toast.Title/Toast.Description plus a Toast.Close 'Dismiss' button, with CSS-only stacking driven by --toast-index/--toast-offset-y/--toast-frontmost-height/--toast-swipe-movement-* variables

name: custom
whatItDemonstrates: A toast carrying typed custom data: the 'Create custom toast' button adds a toast whose `data` option holds { userId: '123' }, and the renderer type-guards on toast.data to display 'data.userId is 123' inside Toast.Description.
stateManaged: none — no local state; the typed payload travels through add()'s `data` option and is read from the toast object while rendering the list
nonTrivialInteractions: a CustomToastData interface plus an isCustomToast type guard (toast.data?.userId !== undefined) narrow Toast.Root.ToastObject to Toast.Root.ToastObject<CustomToastData>
the list renderer branches on the guard: a Description interpolating toast.data.userId when the toast carries custom data, otherwise an empty <Toast.Description />
Toast.Title renders explicit children {toast.title} instead of relying on the default title injection
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.

name: deduplicate
whatItDemonstrates: A deduplicated 'Draft saved' toast: re-clicking 'Save draft' upserts the same toast by its fixed id ('save-status') instead of creating a duplicate, and the item alternates CSS pulse-animation classes based on the parity of toast.updateKey so the pulse replays while the toast stays mounted.
stateManaged: none — no local state; the upsert behavior comes entirely from passing a constant id to add() and reading toast.updateKey in the renderer
nonTrivialInteractions: add() with the same id updates the existing toast in place, incrementing its updateKey

PulseToastItem derives the pulse class from toast.updateKey: 0 (first add) renders no pulse class, even updateKey maps to styles.PulseEven and odd to styles.PulseOdd, so consecutive clicks alternate animation names and restart the animation without remounting
the final className is assembled by filtering null out of [styles.Toast, pulseClassName] and joining, keeping the base class always present
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.

name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: The canonical stacked toast queue: a 'Create toast' button adds incrementing-numbered toasts that stack in a fixed bottom-right viewport with CSS-variable-driven collapsed stacking, each toast dismissible via a Toast.Close 'Dismiss' button.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — toasts are created and owned by the provider via useToastManager().add(); a local useState counter is only used to number the titles ('Toast 1 created', 'Toast 2 created', …)
nonTrivialInteractions: the viewport is fixed bottom-right (top-auto, right-[1rem], bottom-[1rem], widened to 22.5rem at the sm breakpoint) and toasts stack via CSS custom props --toast-index/--toast-offset-y/--toast-frontmost-height/--toast-swipe-movement-*
each click increments the local counter before add() so consecutive toasts get unique numbered titles
Toast.Close 'Dismiss' removes its own toast; swipe-to-dismiss transforms and data-expanded/data-behind content fade are handled purely in CSS

name: position
whatItDemonstrates: The same stacked queue as the hero demo but repositioned to the top-center of the screen purely through Viewport/Root CSS, with swipeDirection="up" on Toast.Root so swiping a toast upward dismisses it.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — toasts are created and owned by the provider via useToastManager().add(); a local useState counter only numbers the titles, as in the hero demo
nonTrivialInteractions: the viewport is fixed top-center (top-[1rem], left-0/right-0, mx-auto, max-w 22.5rem, bottom-auto) and toasts stack downward from origin-top using the same CSS custom-prop stack as the hero demo, mirrored for the top edge
Toast.Root swipeDirection="up" enables swipe-to-dismiss in the upward direction and drives the per-direction data-swipe-direction CSS branches
each click increments the local counter before add() so consecutive toasts get unique numbered titles

name: promise
whatItDemonstrates: An asynchronous operation toast: clicking 'Run promise' shows a 'Loading data…' toast that automatically transitions to a success or error description when a 2-second simulated API promise (70% success rate) settles.
stateManaged: none — no local state; the toast's loading/success/error progression is driven entirely by toastManager.promise() receiving the Promise and the per-state description callbacks
nonTrivialInteractions: toastManager.promise() is given a Promise<string> that resolves with 'operation completed' or rejects with Error('operation failed') after a 2000ms setTimeout, with Math.random() > 0.3 deciding the outcome
the shortcut form passes loading as a string and success/error as functions of the settled value/reason, each returning the description string interpolated with the result
the toast list itself is the standard mapped Toast.Root/Content/Title/Description + Toast.Close rendering
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.

name: undo
whatItDemonstrates: An undoable action toast: 'Perform action' adds a success toast with a 10-second timeout and an 'Undo' action button configured via add()'s actionProps, whose onClick closes the original toast by its returned id and adds a follow-up 'Action undone' toast.
stateManaged: none — the toastId returned by add() is captured in a local const and referenced from the actionProps.onClick closure; no component state is involved
nonTrivialInteractions: add() returns a toastId that the actionProps.onClick closure uses to call toastManager.close(id) before adding the confirmation toast { title: 'Action undone' }
actionProps { children: 'Undo', onClick } fully props the <Toast.Action /> rendered inside the list, which itself has no children
type: 'success' combined with timeout: 10000 keeps the toast visible long enough to undo
the list nests Title/Description in a message column beside Toast.Action
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.

name: varying-heights
whatItDemonstrates: Stacking toasts of heterogeneous sizes: each click picks a random description from four texts of increasing length so the collapsed stack demonstrates the --toast-frontmost-height height clamp, with full content revealed when the viewport expands on hover or focus.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — toasts are created and owned by the provider via useToastManager().add(); a local useState counter only numbers the titles, as in the hero demo
nonTrivialInteractions: each click picks a random entry from the TEXTS array (four descriptions from 'Short message.' up to a multi-line sentence) so every toast gets a different height

while collapsed, every toast's height is clamped to the frontmost toast's height via the --toast-frontmost-height/--toast-height CSS variables; hovering or focusing the viewport expands them and the data-behind content fades back in
each click increments the local counter before add() so consecutive toasts get unique numbered titles
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.
